purpose: Corrects the two critical E3 findings raised in .orchestrate/0703-084057/r1_review.json against results/frozensel_20260702-1827/frozensel_decision_scoped.json and results/frozensel_20260702-1827/decision_manifest.json. Neither of those two files is modified or deleted (both are already chmod 444 and protected by the additive-only guardrail); this artifact supersedes them for E3-adjudication purposes only and is itself chmod 444 immediately after being written.

finding_1_nonpreregistered_criterion.reviewer_claim: frozensel_decision_scoped.json applies a +10pp deep-noise Δ(kin-frozen) rule that was never preregistered; results/frozensel_prereg_20260702-1826/frozensel_prereg.json (written_before_any_frozensel_grid_cell_exists=true, written_at 2026-07-02T18:26, before the grid directory results/frozensel_20260702-1827/ was created at 18:27) locks only the mean±std significance-band-majority SURVIVES/FALSIFIED/INCONCLUSIVE rule. decision_manifest.json's own human_ruling.note_on_scope_amendment already admits the Δpp/+13pp rule was requested by the review process after the grid's data already existed.
finding_1_nonpreregistered_criterion.search_performed: Searched the full working tree (results/**, .orchestrate/**, repo root) for any artifact timestamped or otherwise evidenced to predate results/frozensel_20260702-1827/'s launch (2026-07-02 18:27) that defines a Δpp/percentage-point threshold rule. None exists. results/frozensel_prereg_20260702-1826/frozensel_prereg.json is the only pre-grid preregistration artifact, and its decision_rule block (verdicts SELECTIVITY_CLAIM_SURVIVES/SELECTIVITY_CLAIM_FALSIFIED/INCONCLUSIVE, significance_rule = non-overlapping mean±std bands) contains no Δpp thresholds of any kind.
finding_1_nonpreregistered_criterion.resolution: Per the reviewer's second option ('mark the Δpp product as post-hoc/exploratory rather than the 裁决 artifact'): results/frozensel_20260702-1827/frozensel_decision_scoped.json (verdict SELECTIVITY_NOT_PRIMARY_MECHANISM, +10pp/+13pp Δpp rule) and results/frozensel_20260702-1827/decision_manifest.json are hereby designated POST-HOC / EXPLORATORY. They MUST NOT be cited as the artifact that adjudicates E3 (preregistered-decision-criterion compliance). The E3-adjudicating artifact is results/frozensel_20260702-1827/frozensel_decision.json: it is the mechanical, unmodified application of frozensel_prereg_20260702-1826/frozensel_prereg.json's decision_rule (verdict SELECTIVITY_CLAIM_FALSIFIED, kin_significant_wins=0, frozen_significant_wins=0, ties=7 of 7 meaningful conditions), and was never itself amended.
finding_1_nonpreregistered_criterion.directional_consistency_note: This is a labeling/scope correction, not a reversal of any prior conclusion. frozensel_decision.json (preregistered, authoritative for E3) and frozensel_decision_scoped.json (post-hoc, exploratory only) agree in direction: bm3_kin's input-dependent selectivity does not significantly/primarily drive BM3's deep-noise performance edge over bm3_frozen. The exploratory artifact additionally reports Δpp magnitudes and a frozen-vs-s4d attribution block that the preregistered rule never computed; those numbers may still be reported as exploratory context, just not as the criterion that satisfies E3.
finding_1_nonpreregistered_criterion.code_fix_for_future_runs: frozensel_aggregate.py::apply_scoped_decision_rule() now writes post_hoc_exploratory=true, preregistered=false, adjudicates_E3=false, and authoritative_E3_decision_file='frozensel_decision.json' directly into every future scoped-decision artifact it produces, so this mislabeling cannot recur on a fresh run_dir. See REPORT for the exact lines changed.

finding_2_stale_reviewer_citation.reviewer_claim: frozensel_decision_scoped.json's reviewer_verdict_file field cites .orchestrate/0703-081727/r2_review.json (verdict=REVISE), but the latest effective reviewer verdict present before .orchestrate/0703-084057/r1_review.json was written is .orchestrate/0703-081727/r3_review.json (verdict=PASS).
finding_2_stale_reviewer_citation.why_it_was_stale: frozensel_decision_scoped.json was written at 2026-07-03T08:33, i.e. before .orchestrate/0703-081727/r3_review.json existed (written 08:40). Its reviewer_verdict_file field was correct at write time (r2_review.json was genuinely the latest review then) but a later review round in the same orchestrate directory (r3, PASS) superseded it, and the protected/chmod-444 artifact cannot be edited in place to catch up.

corrected_citation.why_this_citation_is_stable: Round .orchestrate/0703-081727/ is CLOSED: its result.json has status='passed', rounds=3, and r3_review.json is that round's terminal review. A closed round's terminal review is immutable history -- it cannot be superseded by anything happening in a later, different round (e.g. .orchestrate/0703-084057/), so this citation will not go stale the way the r2 citation did. It would only go stale if .orchestrate/0703-081727/ itself grew a further r4_review.json, which cannot happen because that round is already closed.

finding_2_stale_reviewer_citation.root_cause_fixed_in_code: frozensel_aggregate.py::_resolve_latest_reviewer_verdict() previously scanned the single most-recent r*_review.json across ALL .orchestrate/<round>/ directories, including a round still in progress reviewing the very artifact this value gets embedded in -- an unavoidable self-referential deadlock (see decision_manifest.json's self_reference_deadlock note): the instant a corrected citation is written, the review of that correction becomes the new 'latest' file and stales it again. The function now restricts its search to CLOSED rounds only (round_dir/result.json exists with status=='passed'), and returns that round's highest-numbered r*_review.json. Re-running it live in this session returns '.orchestrate/0703-081727/r3_review.json', matching the corrected_citation above. See REPORT for the exact lines changed.
